target.title: Improve memory recall ranking
target.body:
﻿## Summary

Adds a focused memory recall ranking hardening pass inspired by MnemoCore-style long-tail memory behavior, while keeping public memory-search contracts stable:

- tokenize Unicode recall terms and diacritic-folded variants for better multilingual recall
- bound and deduplicate FTS recall queries
- stabilize hybrid score tie ordering
- sanitize MMR lambda config
- document existing recall ranking knobs
- removed the previously proposed `temporalDecay.minMultiplier` public config knob
- removed surfaced score diagnostics from results so `MemorySearchResult` shape remains unchanged
- rebased onto current `origin/main`

## Real behavior / ranking proof

Compared current `origin/main` and this PR head through memory-core ranking entrypoints with a temporary real workspace containing dated `memory/*.md` files.

```json
{
  "node": "v24.16.0",
  "repoBase": "origin/main",
  "prHead": "agent/memory-recall-ranking",
  "workspace": "temp memory/*.md dated files",
  "datedRankingCompatibility": {
    "before": [
      {
        "path": "memory/2026-02-10.md",
        "score": 0.886,
        "vectorScore": 0.88,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "recent rollback keyword"
      },
      {
        "path": "memory/projects.md",
        "score": 0.886,
        "vectorScore": 0.88,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "evergreen keyword"
      },
      {
        "path": "memory/2024-01-01.md",
        "score": 0,
        "vectorScore": 0.92,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "old rollback keyword"
      }
    ],
    "after": [
      {
        "path": "memory/2026-02-10.md",
        "score": 0.886,
        "vectorScore": 0.88,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "recent rollback keyword"
      },
      {
        "path": "memory/projects.md",
        "score": 0.886,
        "vectorScore": 0.88,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "evergreen keyword"
      },
      {
        "path": "memory/2024-01-01.md",
        "score": 0,
        "vectorScore": 0.92,
        "textScore": 0.9,
        "snippet": "old rollback keyword"
      }
    ],
    "behaviorEqual": true
  },
  "deterministicTieRanking": {
    "beforeOrder": [
      "memory/b.md",
      "memory/a.md"
    ],
    "afterOrder": [
      "memory/a.md",
      "memory/b.md"
    ]
  },
  "ftsCap": {
    "beforeTokenCount": 40,
    "afterTokenCount": 32,
    "afterLastToken": "\"term31\""
  },
  "publicResultKeys": [
    "endLine",
    "path",
    "score",
    "snippet",
    "source",
    "startLine",
    "textScore",
    "vectorScore"
  ],
  "publicContractStable": true
}
```

Interpretation:
- Existing temporal-decay ranking behavior remains identical for the exercised dated-memory workspace.
- Tie ordering is now deterministic instead of depending on insertion order.
- Oversized FTS queries are capped to 32 tokens, avoiding unbounded MATCH query growth.
- Public result keys remain the existing `MemorySearchResult` surface; no `scoreBeforeTemporalDecay` or `temporalDecayMultiplier` fields are surfaced.

## Validation

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo

$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/concepts/memory-search.md docs/reference/memory-config.md extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/temporal-decay.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/temporal-decay.ts src/agents/memory-search.test.ts src/agents/memory-search.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.help.ts src/config/schema.labels.ts src/config/types.tools.ts src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

## Compatibility / maintainer decision

This revision follows the recommended split-and-defer path from ClawSweeper:

- no new `temporalDecay.minMultiplier` config surface
- no new observable score diagnostic result fields
- no schema, migration, vector metadata format, embedding content, or stored data-model changes
- remaining changes are ranking hardening and docs/tests around existing behavior
